newsitem.title: FRANCE: French activists protest against town begging ban.
newsitem.headline: French activists protest against town begging ban.

text.p: French civil rights activists protested on Saturday against a ban on begging in the town of Millau, imposed by mayor Jacques Godefrain, France's Minister for Overseas Cooperation.
Up to 1,000 demonstrators from around France marched in Millau, one of several southern towns which outlawed begging or sitting or lying in the streets at the start of the tourist season this year.
Municipal authorities said the number of homeless people who harassed visitors was unacceptably high, but protesters said the ban aimed at driving poor people and hippies out of town.
There were no incidents during the march led by Professor Leon Schwartzenberg, a former Socialist health minister and champion of the homeless as well as of illegal African immigrants.
Activists chose Millau for the demonstration since Godefrain, a conservative, is the only one of the mayors who imposed such bans to hold cabinet rank.
